slides.0.title: Central Valley I: Maipo and Cachapoal
slides.0.subtitle: The heartland of Chilean Cabernet and the northern half of Rapel
slides.1.title: Maipo Valley at a glance
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Just south of Santiago at roughly 33–34°S, bisected by the Maipo River and running from the Andes to the Coastal Cordillera (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Home of Cabernet
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth: seen as the heartland of Chilean Cabernet Sauvignon, with Cabernet over 60% of plantings and about 11,000 ha in total, plus Carmenère, Merlot, Syrah and Cabernet Franc
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sub-DOs
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Puente Alto, Pirque, Buin, Isla de Maipo, Talagante and María Pinto (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: Maipo is the closest region to the capital and the most emblematic home of Cabernet.
slides.2.title: Maipo's terroir
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Climate
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A Mediterranean climate with hot dry summers and cool wet winters; 300–400 mm of rain a year, mostly May to August, with irrigation from Andean snowmelt (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Soils
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Alto Maipo's piedmont has rounded river gravels, sand and a little clay, free-draining and low in organic matter; the central part has water-retentive clay-loam (Wine With Seth); Decanter calls the soils around Puente Alto very stony
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Day-night swing
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The ripening-season swing is about 15–18°C (Wine With Seth); Decanter says large swings help phenolic ripeness
slides.2.content: Maipo is a Cabernet terroir of piedmont gravels and wide day-night swings.
slides.3.title: Maipo's history and icons
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Old houses
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Cousiño-Macul (1856), Santa Rita (1880, in Buin) and Concha y Toro (1883, in Pirque) (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Icon wines
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Don Melchor's first vintage was 1987 (released 1990); Almaviva was founded in 1996 as a 50/50 venture of Concha y Toro and Baron Philippe de Rothschild; Viñedo Chadwick's first vintage was 1999 (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The Berlin tasting (single source)
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth records a January 2004 Berlin tasting in which Chadwick 2000 placed first, ahead of Lafite 2000 and Margaux 2001, with Seña 2001 second
slides.3.content: Maipo's old houses and icon wines put Chilean Cabernet on the world stage.
slides.4.title: Cachapoal: the northern half of Rapel
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.4.highlights.0.content: The northern half of the Rapel Valley DO, between Maipo and Colchagua at about 34°S, with Rancagua in the central depression (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Scale and grapes
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth: about 10,800 ha with Cabernet Sauvignon over 40%; the transversal zones are Andes (500–900 m), Entre Cordilleras (350–500 m) and Costa (around Peumo and Las Cabras), though figures differ between sources
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Signatures
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Peumo is known for Carmenère (Concha y Toro's Carmín de Peumo, first vintage 1996); Altaïr (2001) and Vik (2004) are also here (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.content: Cachapoal is Rapel's northern half, and Peumo Carmenère is its calling card.
Which of these is not a Maipo sub-DO?
Apalta is in the Colchagua area.
Maipo's most important red grape is?
Cabernet is over 60% of plantings (Wine With Seth).
Almaviva is a joint venture of which two parties?
A. Concha y Toro and Baron Philippe de Rothschild
Which two valleys make up the Rapel Valley DO?
Cachapoal is the northern half and Colchagua the southern.
Which variety is Cachapoal's Peumo known for?
For example Concha y Toro's Carmín de Peumo.
